summary: R. Ramanujachari was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and edited the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. An Indologist, he taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984), served as President of the Indian Music Congress, and instructed Andrey Klebanov, R. S. Nandakumar, and Srikantham Nagendra Shastry.
R. T. Vyas is an Indologist who served as General Editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara from 1993 to 1994.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000), a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. His career included posts at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, ICPR, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

R. Venkatraman works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and served there as Reader (attested 1990).

Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School (~1875–1876) and University College London (~1878–1880). He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

Rachael Margaret Griffiths specializes in Tibetology and computational studies. She earned her DPhil from the University of Oxford by 2020, held a postdoc at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023), and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2024).
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York. In 2023, she served as Reader at the University of Liverpool.

Rachel H. Pang is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia and was Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachel Van Meter Baumer (1928–1995) was an Indologist who studied under Thomas Welbourne Clark and completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1958–1964). She taught at Michigan State University, University of Minnesota, and University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Rachelle M. Scott works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and joined the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, where she was appointed Associate Professor in 2002.

Rade Uhlik (1899–1991) was a linguist and Indologist who studied Germanistics at the University of Belgrade. He worked as a translator for Tanjug and as a custos at the National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina (~1953).

Radha Burnier (1923–2013) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at Kalakshetra and Banaras Hindu University. She served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre from approximately 1960 to 1980.

Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985), an Indologist and historian, studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. He founded the K. P. Jayaswal Archaeological Museum and held posts at Ganesh Dutt College, Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University.

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1901–1905). He held positions at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917), the University of Mysore, and Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1917–1921).

Radhey Kishori is a scholar in Indology and computational fields. She taught at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra, Dr. MPS Group of Institutions, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi, and the Institute of Innovation in Technology and Management.

Radhika Herzberger (1938–) is an Indologist and philosopher. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto (~1974–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal and served as Director of Rishi Valley School (~1982–2012).

Radoslav Katičić (1930–2019) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Zagreb and under Paul Thieme (~1956–1958). He was a professor at the University of Vienna (~1977–1998) and a member of the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts.

Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure, and held visiting appointments at Wadham College (2012–2013) and Harvard University (attested 2015).

Rafał Felbur is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University (attested 2015), where he was supervised by Paul Harrison (attested 2018), and also studied under John R. McRae and Luis Oscar Gómez.
